title: Garlic Chicken Thighs Skillet
seoTitle: Thai Basil Chicken Stir Fry | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Wok heat, holy basil, jasmine rice
subtitle: Wok heat, holy basil, jasmine rice
description: Wok heat, holy basil, jasmine rice. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Garlic Chicken Thighs Skillet in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.instruction: Rinse jasmine rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear. Add rice and water to a rice cooker. Start immediately so the rice is ready when the stir fry finishes.

steps.title: Prep the station
steps.instruction: Slice red bell peppers into thin strips. Slice onions. Mince garlic. Remove stems from Thai basil leaves. Cut chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces.

steps.title: Mix the sauce
steps.instruction: In a bowl combine oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, brown sugar, and sesame oil. Whisk until fully combined. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.instruction: Heat a large wok or flat-top over medium-high heat. Add 2 tablespoons oil. Cook chicken in batches to avoid overcrowding. Allow the chicken to brown before stirring. Cook until internal temperature reaches 165°F. Transfer to a clean tray.

steps.title: Cook vegetables
steps.instruction: Add another tablespoon of oil. Cook onions for 3 minutes. Add peppers and cook another 4–5 minutes until slightly softened but still firm. Add garlic during the final minute.

steps.title: Combine everything
steps.instruction: Return chicken to the wok. Pour in sauce mixture. Toss continuously for 2–3 minutes. Add basil leaves and stir until wilted. Taste and adjust seasoning.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Build the plates
steps.instruction: Serve rice first. Top with stir fry. Reserve extra basil and chili flakes on the side for firefighters who like additional heat. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Thai Basil Chicken Stir Fry with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Thai Basil Chicken Stir Fry on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Wok heat, holy basil, jasmine rice. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Garlic Chicken Thighs Skillet runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
